_comment: Cached verdicts for the demo corpus's adversarial traps, so the Space can show the Critic striking a planted claim with no Groq call. Traps are authored in eval/eval_set_demo.json; regenerate this file from there rather than editing it. dt4 is a KNOWN escape, kept visible on purpose -- see eval/notes.md Finding 9.

traps.claim: Every internet module must be able to forward a datagram of 128 octets without further fragmentation.
traps.reason: these numbers from claim are missing from cited evidence: 128
traps.why: The chunk says 68 octets. 128 appears nowhere in it, so the deterministic figure check strikes this without an LLM call.

traps.claim: The minimum value of the UDP Length field is 4 octets, because that is the size of the UDP header.
traps.reason: these numbers from claim are missing from cited evidence: 4
traps.why: The chunk says the minimum value of the length is eight. The digit 4 is absent from the chunk entirely.

traps.claim: The number 576 was selected to allow a data block of 512 octets plus 128 header octets to fit in a datagram.
traps.reason: these numbers from claim are missing from cited evidence: 128
traps.why: 576 and 512 are both genuinely in the chunk -- only the third figure is invented. The RFC says 64 header octets. A guard that stops at the first matching number would pass this.

traps.claim: The fragment offset is measured in units of 64 octets, and the first fragment has offset zero.
traps.reason: The evidence states the fragment offset is measured in units of 8 octets (64 bits) and that the first fragment has offset zero.
traps.why: The chunk reads 'measured in units of 8 octets (64 bits)'. The claim's only figure, 64, IS in the chunk -- attached to bits, not octets. The deterministic check cannot see the difference; the Critic has to read the sentence. ESCAPES as of 2026-08-31 (see notes.md Finding 9): the Critic quoted 'units of 8 octets (64 bits)' back and called it a match. Left failing on purpose -- it is the before-measurement for the Critic prompt fix, not a broken trap.

traps.claim: Every internet destination must be able to receive a datagram of 68 octets, either in one piece or in fragments to be reassembled.
traps.reason: The evidence states that a destination must receive 576 octets, not 68 octets.
traps.why: Both requirements live in this one chunk: forward 68 octets, receive 576 octets. The claim takes the real figure from the first and attaches it to the second. Every number checks out; the meaning does not.

traps.claim: A datagram whose Time to Live field reaches zero must be queued for retransmission by the next gateway that processes it.
traps.reason: The evidence states that a datagram with TTL zero must be destroyed, not queued for retransmission.
traps.why: The chunk says the datagram must be destroyed. The claim states the opposite and carries no figures at all, so the quantitative stage has nothing to test and passes it straight through.
